newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton mixed in light trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton mixed in light trade.

text.p: Indian cotton was mixed on Friday with Punjab varieties range-bound while Gujarat varieties rose, dealers said.
Punjab cotton was steady in light trade while Gujarat varieties moved up on shortage of ready stock and increased demand from mills, dealers said.
In spot deals Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) rose 200 rupees to 13,700/14,200 rupees per candy (355.56 kgs).
"Shortage of good quality cotton has led to mills switching from Punjab cotton to Gujarat varieties," one dealer said.
Punjab cotton was steady in light trade despite reports that arrivals in the Punjab region had fallen to 1,500/2,000 bales (170 kg each) per day.
In spot deals Punjab saw-ginned was steady at 1,600/1,700 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while F-414 was unchanged at 1,910/1,930 rupees per maund.
Bengal-deshi was steady at its previous level of 885/935 rupees per maund.
